Study a PhD in a department dedicated to exploring the latest research from advanced sensors and bio-technologies to power, and radio and acoustic waves.
We offer research programmes in a variety of areas based on the work being carried out by our research centres:
Centre for Bioengineering & Biomedical Technologies
Centre for Climate Adaptation & Environment Research (CAER)
Centre for Integrated Materials, Processes & Structures (IMPS)
Centre for Regenerative Design & Engineering for a Net-Positive World (RENEW)
Centre for Sustainable Energy Systems (SES)
IAAPS research
Centre for Digital, Manufacturing & Design (The Foundry)
You'll be welcomed into the Department as a junior academic colleague rather than a student. We expect you to play a full and professional role in contributing to the Departmentâs objective of international academic excellence.
Find out more about our research
Programme structure
Most students complete this programme in 4 years. You cannot take less than 2 years to finish your research and the maximum time you are allowed is normally 4 years.
You can start this programme in September or October.
You may also start mid-year, subject to agreement with your supervisor and the Doctoral College.
Occasionally we make changes to our programmes in response to, for example, feedback from students, developments in research and the field of studies, and the requirements of accrediting bodies. You will be advised of any significant changes to the advertised programme, in accordance with our Terms and Conditions.
Your academic progress and general welfare will be monitored by your supervisor.

Research content
Youâll join the Department as a member of the research centre that best fits your broad research interest and as agreed on acceptance.
Most of our research students register as probationers for the PhD programme to begin with. Your PhD registration is confirmed subject to your passing an assessment process. This normally involves submitting written work and an oral examination.
Professional Development
Professional development is a crucial element of doctoral study, not only in supporting your research but also as part of your longer term career development. Our MyDoctoralDevelopment workshops and courses will help you build your skills and help you succeed in your doctorate.
Read more about professional development support
Assessment
Assessment methods
Thesis
Viva Voce
Assessment description
We expect you to carry out supervised research at the forefront of your chosen subject, which must then be written up as a substantial thesis. Presenting your research findings is an important part of research training so we encourage you to prepare papers for publication throughout your PhD.
The final stage of the PhD programme is the oral or viva voce examination, where you must defend your thesis to a Board of Examiners.
Entry requirements
Academic requirements
A strong academic background in a field relevant to the proposed research, specifically:
A first-class or upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), or
A masterâs degree with a minimum of a merit classification (or equivalent)
Some academic-led research projects may have further requirements which will be stipulated in individual project advertisements.
English Language requirements
If English isnât your first language, youâll need to meet the minimum English language requirements before you can start your course.
Youâll need to provide us with a valid result in an approved English language test, for example:
Duolingo: 120 overall with sub scores of Speaking 110, Writing 110, Reading 110, Listening 105
Academic IELTS: 6.5 overall with no less than 6.0 in any component
TOEFL iBT or TOEFL iBT Home Edition (taken before 21 January 2026): 90 overall with no less than 21 in any element
TOEFL iBT or TOEFL iBT Home Edition (taken after 20 January 2026): 4.5 overall with no less than 4.0 in any component
See the required scores for all the English language tests we accept.
You must have taken your English language qualification within 24 months of your course start date.
If you need to improve your English language skills before starting your studies, you might be able to take aâ¯pre-sessional courseâ¯to reach the required level.
You don't normally need to provide evidence of your English language proficiency if:
you're a UK national
you're a national of a majority English-speaking country, as recognised by UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI), and youâve lived and been educated in that country for a significant period
you hold a degree taught in English awarded within two years of your course start date
References
Two references are required. At least one of these should be an academic reference from the most recent place of study.
Fees and funding
Fees and funding information for Electronic and Electrical Engineering PhD
Fees
Your tuition fees and how you pay them will depend on whether you are a Home or Overseas student.
Learn how we decide fee status
Tuition fees are liable to increase annually for all University of Bath students.
If you aren't paying your fees in British pounds, you should also budget for possible fluctuations in your own currency.
Find out more about student fees
Extra costs
You will need to budget for living expenses and, if you donât already live in Bath, your relocation costs.
The University has developed some resources to help you understand typical costs of living in Bath. Please see the example postgraduate budget or the example budget for an overseas student intending to bring family to Bath.
If you require a visa to study in the UK, you will also need to budget for visa fees and the Immigration Healthcare surcharge (IHS).
Some PhD projects necessitate payment of a Training Support Fee (sometimes known as a Bench Fee) in addition to tuition fees. Your intended PhD project supervisor will be able to advise if this will apply to your intended PhD project.
Find out more about Training Support Fees (TSF)

Application deadline
3 months prior to the intended start date (for international applicants) or 2 months prior to the intended start date (for home applicants). For example, for an end of September start, the deadline is 30 June (international) and 31 July (home).
Regulator
The Office for Students (OfS)
Applicant profile
We seek applications from outstanding individuals from anywhere in the world. You should be strongly committed to carrying out high-quality academic research in any of the disciplinary areas covered by our research centres.
A competitive applicant profile will show:
Strong academic credentials
Your readiness to be an independent PhD researcher
A clear understanding of the proposed research project, its intended methods and its aims
Alignment between the applicantâs research interests/experience and the supervisorâs or departmentâs research priorities
Application guidance
You can apply for one of our pre-defined research projects or develop your own proposal. Our academic staff are always open to hear how your research can build on their existing work or about a new topic in their current subject areas.
You must identify at least one (up to two) intended lead supervisor(s) in your application. We cannot consider your application if no supervisor has been named.
To increase your chances of success, we strongly recommend that you contact your intended supervisor(s) ahead of submitting your application to make them aware of your interest and to discuss the intended research project. This applies even if you intend to apply in response to an advertised pre-defined research project. It is especially important if you intend to apply with your own project idea because, in this case, you will need to ensure, firstly, that your research interests are compatible with the expertise of your intended supervisor(s) and, secondly, that they have capacity to take on new PhD students.
If you are applying with your own project idea (as opposed to applying for a pre-defined/advertised research project), you should submit a 1000-word research proposal with your application. Within your proposal you should explain the knowledge gap you have identified, how you intend to fill it, and it should give an indicative timeline of work for discussion with your potential supervisor.
In all cases, in your personal statement, you will need to tell us why you are interested in pursuing independent research, quote examples of your undergraduate or master's research projects, and explain how a PhD fits with your career plans.
See our guide about how to apply for doctoral study for more information and further documents required.
Selection process
When your application is received, it will be forwarded to your intended supervisor(s). If they are interested in pursuing your application, they will ask the Doctoral Admissions team to review your application. This will include assessing your tuition fee status, checking that your application is complete and confirming that you meet the minimum entry criteria as quoted in the âEntry requirementsâ section above.
The outcome of the Doctoral Admissions team review will be sent to your intended supervisor(s) who will then decide if they wish to invite you to interview. Interviews will typically be conducted online by the prospective supervisor(s) and an independent member of academic staff or the Director of Studies.
If you are applying to one of our funding competitions, there may be further shortlisting and decision stages which will be competition specific.
It is important to remember that PhD places are competitively awarded and your application will be considered as a whole including the quality of all your uploaded documents and your references as well as your ability to meet entry requirements and demonstrate relevant research experience/potential.
Immigration requirements
This PhD is covered by the UK Foreign & Commonwealth Office (FCO) Academic Technology Approval Scheme (ATAS). If you are an international student, you may require an ATAS certificate to join this course and you can find out more about the visa requirements for studying in the UK.
For additional support please contact the Student Immigration Service for matters related to student visas and immigration.
